 Food Bank of Wyoming partnering with Smith’s Food and Drug for food drive this holiday season 
 by 
 Nick Perkins 
 4 hours ago November 4, 2026 
 Share this:

 Photo Courtesy of the Food Bank of Wyoming 
 GILLETTE, Wyo. — The Food Bank of Wyoming recently announced that it is partnering with Smith’s Food and Drug to host a community food drive across Wyoming.
 A release from the Food Bank of Wyoming says the food drive is happening Nov. 1–15 in a multitude of cities statewide.
 “Together with community partners, Food Bank of Wyoming and its network of Hunger Relief Partners are helping feed neighbors this Thanksgiving,” the release states. “With 1 in 6 people in Wyoming facing hunger and food costs rising, community support is critical. Food Bank of Wyoming emphasizes the power of collaboration in addressing food insecurity this holiday season and shares ways to get involved.”
 The release says that each Smith’s store in Wyoming is partnering with a local hunger relief organization and food collected at each store will go to that specific partner for distribution to local neighbors throughout the holiday season.
 Stores and partners include:
 Evanston Smith’s, 70 Yellowcreek Road – Lord’s Storehouse
 Gillette Smith’s, 906 Camel Drive – Council of Community Services
 Riverton Smith’s, 1200 W. Main St. – 477 and Sweetgrass Food Lodge
 Casper Smith’s, 2405 CY Ave. – Joshua’s Storehouse and The Salvation Army
 Rock Springs Smith’s, 2531 Foothill Blvd. — Food Bank of Sweetwater County
 Jackson Hole Smith’s, 1425 Wyoming Highway 89 South — One22
 Green River Smith’s, 905 Bridger Drive – Food Bank of Sweetwater County
 Customers and community members can participate in the drive by bringing nonperishable food items to their local Smith’s or by purchasing extra items at the checkout line.
 “When you think of the holidays, you think of time with family and eating delicious food,” says Lisette Saldaña-Capulet, Smith’s communications and public affairs manager. “We hope this food drive can help families in need keep their Thanksgiving traditions alive with a little help from their community and Smith’s.”
 Additionally, this year, Smith’s is donating 100 hams to the Food Bank of Wyoming’s Hunger Relief Partners, Joshua’s Storehouse, and The Salvation Army in Casper in order to support the annual Thanksgiving Food Distribution.
 “We hope that families facing food insecurity can go to their local food bank or pantry to collect items so they can take part in Thanksgiving celebrations with their loved ones,” Saldaña-Capulet says. “We also hope that this food drive shows the community that when they partner with Smith’s to donate, they can count on the food staying local, so it helps a neighbor in need.”
 The release notes that one of the best ways for individuals to support the Food Bank of Wyoming during this time of year is to donate financially. Every dollar helps provide enough food for three meals. 
 Additionally, volunteering can help put food on people’s plates this year . Whether people build food boxes at the Casper Distribution Center or engage in a To-Go Volunteer Project in one’s area, donated time helps make a difference to those in need.
 “More of our Wyoming neighbors are facing food insecurity, and we know the holidays can bring added financial pressure for families,” says Olivia McCarthy, Food Bank of Wyoming’s director of development. “By coming together, we can make our resources go further, strengthen our community, and help families get the food they need to share good meals and create meaningful memories.”
